title: What is the difference between stress and burnout?

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚到除了出卖时间换取金钱之外的收入，会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性的收入来源。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有个好消息要宣布。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己曾在2022年完成了该项目，此后也支持了两批心理学家走过他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖励，以及我提供的独家支持套餐，无需额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四次小组智囊团会议、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特纳姆和梅森的礼品，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过描述中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时为你解答。

sentences.en: Coming up today, what is the difference between stress and burnout?
sentences.zh: 今天我们要讨论的话题是：压力和倦怠之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: How might we recognize that in ourselves?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何识别自己身上的这些状态？

sentences.en: And how might we help our clients to understand that too?
sentences.zh: 我们又该如何帮助我们的客户理解这一点？

sentences.en: That is the topic of today's episode.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天这一集的主题。

sentences.en: I hope you find this so useful.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得这非常有帮助。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听《有抱负的心理学家》播客。

sentences.en: I am Dr. Marianne Trent and I'm a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安·特伦特博士，我是一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: This is part of a series of episodes called Burnout Bites, which is being hosted for me, for us.
sentences.zh: 这是名为“倦怠小知识”系列节目的一部分，由克莱尔·普拉姆利博士为我、为我们主持。

sentences.en: By Dr. Claire Plumley, who is incredible.
sentences.zh: 她非常出色。

sentences.en: She is the author of a brand new book all about burnout.
sentences.zh: 她刚刚出版了一本关于倦怠的新书。

sentences.en: And you can learn more about that in the show notes.
sentences.zh: 你可以在节目说明中了解更多相关信息。

sentences.en: I really want to model to you guys, whoever you are, whether you are listening because you work in mental health and you're an aspiring psychologist,
sentences.zh: 我真的很想为你们树立榜样，无论你是谁，无论你是为了从事心理健康工作而收听，还是因为你是一位有抱负的心理学家，

sentences.en: or whether you're listening because you have an interest in your mental health or that of someone that you care about.
sentences.zh: 或者你是因为对自己的心理健康或你关心的人的心理健康感兴趣而收听。

sentences.en: I want you to know that it's always okay to ask for help, never makes you look weak, and it's always a great thing to do.
sentences.zh: 我想让你知道，寻求帮助永远是可以的，这绝不会让你显得软弱，而且这总是一件很棒的事情。

sentences.en: And that's what I am modeling with this special podcast series.
sentences.zh: 这就是我通过这个特别播客系列所要传达的榜样。

sentences.en: They are all standalone episodes, but they are all grouped together under the term of burnout, or should I say anti-burnout.
sentences.zh: 它们都是独立的剧集，但都归类在“倦怠”这个主题下，或者我应该说“反倦怠”。

sentences.en: And it's a really, really brilliant fit for this podcast, because if you're a long-term listener,
sentences.zh: 这与本播客非常契合，因为如果你是长期听众，

sentences.en: you will know that I often ask people at the end of the podcast what their top tip for reducing burnout is.
sentences.zh: 你就会知道，我经常在播客结束时问嘉宾他们减少倦怠的秘诀是什么。

sentences.en: So I love that we've got Dr. Claire talking us through this in more detail.
sentences.zh: 所以我很高兴能有克莱尔博士为我们详细讲解这一点。

sentences.en: I will look forward to catching up with you on the other side of this.
sentences.zh: 我很期待在节目之后与你再次交流。

sentences.en: Hello, and welcome back to Burnout Bites.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎回到“倦怠小知识”。

sentences.en: This is a short series of episodes where I'm talking all about burnout,
sentences.zh: 这是一个简短的系列节目，我将在这里讨论关于倦怠的一切，

sentences.en: in the hope that you can learn a little bit more about this topic to keep yourself as safe as possible from it, and of course, the people you work with as well.
sentences.zh: 希望你能多了解这个话题，从而尽可能保护自己，当然也包括保护你共事的人。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Claire Plumley.
sentences.zh: 我是克莱尔·普拉姆利博士。

sentences.en: I'm a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是一名临床心理学家。

sentences.en: I work with people who have gone through traumatic events, feeling anxious, and feeling burned out.
sentences.zh: 我的工作对象是那些经历过创伤事件、感到焦虑和倦怠的人。

sentences.en: I've also written a book recently, and it is out now.
sentences.zh: 我最近也写了一本书，现在已经出版了。

sentences.en: It's on this topic.
sentences.zh: 它就是关于这个主题的。

sentences.en: Burnout is called Burnout, How to Manage Your Nervous System Before It Manages You.
sentences.zh: 这本书叫《倦怠：在神经系统掌控你之前如何掌控它》。

sentences.en: There's a link in the show notes to the book sales page.
sentences.zh: 节目说明中有一个通往售书页面的链接。

sentences.en: So in this episode, we're going to talk about the difference between stress and burnout.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这一集中，我们将讨论压力和倦怠之间的区别。

sentences.en: Often those words might be used interchangeably, so it's helpful to get a distinction between the two.
sentences.zh: 通常这两个词可能会被混用，所以区分两者很有帮助。

sentences.en: I know I'm preaching to the converted when I say that not all stress is bad, and our body is designed for stress.
sentences.zh: 我知道我在班门弄斧，但我还是要说，并非所有的压力都是坏事，我们的身体就是为应对压力而设计的。

sentences.en: We have this amazing bit of kit, our autonomic nervous system, that in an ideal world would shift between its gear settings quite fluidly.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有这套神奇的装备——自主神经系统，在理想情况下，它能在各种档位之间流畅切换。

sentences.en: When we're in our sympathetic nervous system gear, this is an energised, motivated place.
sentences.zh: 当我们处于交感神经系统档位时，这是一种充满活力、积极进取的状态。

sentences.en: We might move from being in that ventral vagal parasympathetic branch, often known as green mode or rest and digest,
sentences.zh: 我们可能会从腹侧迷走神经副交感神经分支（通常被称为“绿色模式”或“休息与消化”）切换出来，

sentences.en: into this kind of sixth gear where everything might feel a little bit more urgent.
sentences.zh: 进入一种类似“六档”的状态，一切都可能感觉更加紧迫。

sentences.en: We get this urge to fix and get stuff done.
sentences.zh: 我们会有解决问题和完成任务的冲动。

sentences.en: We get more racing thoughts.
sentences.zh: 我们的思绪会变得更加纷乱。

sentences.en: And of course, we get the other allostatic changes, so the changes in our body systems, to prepare us for that fight or flight response.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们还会经历其他的异位平衡变化，即身体系统的变化，为“战斗或逃跑”反应做好准备。

sentences.en: Types of changes I'm talking about, again, I know you already know this, and I'm sure it's your bread and butter with your own clients,
sentences.zh: 我所说的这些变化，我知道你们已经很了解了，我相信这在你们与客户的工作中也是家常便饭，

sentences.en: but it's your increased heart rate, it's the tense muscles, it's the shift of digestion into just essential mode.
sentences.zh: 比如心率加快、肌肉紧张、消化系统转入仅维持基本功能的模式。

sentences.en: And of course, our body isn't designed to stay in that gear for too long.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们的身体并不适合长时间保持在那种档位。

sentences.en: We should come back to our rest and digest mode so that our body functions can resume business as normal.
sentences.zh: 我们应该回到“休息与消化”模式，以便身体功能恢复正常运作。

sentences.en: If those sympathetic changes carry on for too long, then this allostatic load builds up.
sentences.zh: 如果那些交感神经的变化持续太久，这种异位负荷就会累积。

sentences.en: But what's more is that our attempts to try and flee or fight the situation, if they continue but the chronic stress just doesn't let up,
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，如果我们试图逃避或对抗这种情况，但如果这种尝试持续存在，而慢性压力却丝毫没有减轻，

sentences.en: then I think what happens is our nervous system dips into the gear that we talk about most in trauma therapy.
sentences.zh: 那么我认为发生的事情是，我们的神经系统会陷入我们在创伤治疗中最常谈论的那个档位。

sentences.en: And this is the dorsal vagal system.
sentences.zh: 这就是背侧迷走神经系统。

sentences.en: This is a part of the nervous system that is more about energy conservation and survival mode.
sentences.zh: 这是神经系统中更多关于能量守恒和生存模式的部分。

sentences.en: So imagine this.
sentences.zh: 所以，想象一下。

sentences.en: Imagine that you are practicing your tennis shots.
sentences.zh: 想象你在练习网球发球。

sentences.en: You're practicing your shots against a tennis ball machine that's throwing the balls at you.
sentences.zh: 你正在对着一台不断向你投球的网球发球机练习。

sentences.en: You've got this, you're hitting the balls back.
sentences.zh: 你应付得来，你把球回击过去。

sentences.en: But hang on a minute, now someone's rolling out a second tennis ball machine.
sentences.zh: 但等一下，现在有人推来了第二台网球发球机。

sentences.en: So now you're having to work at twice the speed.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你必须以两倍的速度工作。

sentences.en: You're hitting double the amount of shots.
sentences.zh: 你回击的球量翻了一倍。

sentences.en: This is the equivalent maybe of stress at work.
sentences.zh: 这可能相当于工作中的压力。

sentences.en: And then maybe there are problems with your children's schooling or things going on at home that you're going to have to deal with as well.
sentences.zh: 然后，也许你的孩子在学校遇到了问题，或者家里还有其他事情需要你处理。

sentences.en: But what if a third machine is pulled out?
sentences.zh: 但如果推来了第三台机器呢？

sentences.en: Maybe this is strains with friendships or maybe you've got utterly parents who need caring for.
sentences.zh: 也许是友谊出现了裂痕，或者你有年迈的父母需要照顾。

sentences.en: This is what a lot of people I work with, and I'm sure you resonate with this in your own personal life,
sentences.zh: 这就是我共事的许多人所经历的，我相信你在自己的个人生活中也会产生共鸣，

sentences.en: go through these times when we have the equivalent of multiple tennis ball machines throwing balls at us.
sentences.zh: 经历这些时刻，我们就像面对多台网球发球机向我们投球一样。

sentences.en: And our attempts to hit these balls back can become quite frenetic.
sentences.zh: 我们回击这些球的尝试可能会变得非常狂乱。

sentences.en: But if there's no let up, we're trying to return the balls, but we're not getting them all.
sentences.zh: 但如果没有喘息的机会，我们试图回球，却无法全部接住。

sentences.en: There's nowhere to escape.
sentences.zh: 无处可逃。

sentences.en: There's no quick exit out the back of the tennis court.
sentences.zh: 网球场后方没有快速出口。

sentences.en: Then we might do the only thing left that's available to us.
sentences.zh: 那么我们可能会采取唯一剩下的办法。

sentences.en: We might curl into a ball to avoid being hurt by these shots as best we can.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会蜷缩成一团，以尽可能避免被这些球击伤。

sentences.en: This is really similar to the learned helplessness idea that you might remember from your training days.
sentences.zh: 这与你培训期间可能记得的“习得性无助”概念非常相似。

sentences.en: This is where we see the symptoms described in burnout.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们看到倦怠症状的地方。

sentences.en: Feeling hollow and like you're on autopilot.
sentences.zh: 感到空虚，就像处于自动驾驶状态一样。

sentences.en: These are all signs that you're not functioning fluidly through your gears and that you either got stuck in that dorsal shutdown
sentences.zh: 这些都是你的神经系统无法流畅切换档位的迹象，要么是你陷入了背侧关闭状态，

sentences.en: or you're oscillating between the sympathetic and the dorsal shutdown without really spending much time in that calmer rest and digest part of your nervous system.
sentences.zh: 要么是在交感神经和背侧关闭状态之间摇摆，而没有在神经系统中更平静的“休息与消化”部分停留太久。

sentences.en: So hopefully this gives you an idea and a framework for understanding the difference between stress in a positive type of stress,
sentences.zh: 所以希望这能为你提供一个理解积极压力（也称为“良性压力”）与导致倦怠的“痛苦”之间区别的框架。

sentences.en: which is also known as eustress, and distress, which tips into burnout.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没接触过，可能需要了解一下。

sentences.en: You might have come across it if you haven't.
sentences.zh: 值得去查阅一下耶基斯-多德森曲线，也称为压力曲线。

sentences.en: It's worthwhile looking up the Yerkes-Dogson curve, also known as the stress curve.
sentences.zh: 它是一条钟形曲线。

sentences.en: It's a bell curve.
sentences.zh: 我也把它收录在我的书中，这是一个相当著名的曲线。

sentences.en: I include it in my book as well, and it's quite a well-known one.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你还不知道它，值得一看。

sentences.en: So if you don't already know it, it's worth taking a look.
sentences.zh: 我在工作中发现，对神经系统的这种理解有助于理解为什么某些技巧对于某些人的当前状态并不适用。

sentences.en: I found in my work that having this understanding of the nervous system has helped to understand why certain techniques aren't quite right for where someone is.
sentences.zh: 例如，通常给倦怠人群的建议非常有道理。

sentences.en: So, for example, the type of advice that is often given for people who are burnt out makes so much sense.
sentences.zh: 我们需要休息。

sentences.en: We need to reSt.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们确实需要。

sentences.en: Absolutely, we do.
sentences.zh: 能帮助我们做到这一点的包括写日记、正念、解决问题的练习、时间块管理、挑战无益的想法等。

sentences.en: And the kind of things that will help us do this is things like journaling, mindfulness, exercises to problem solve and time block, challenging, unhelpful thoughts.
sentences.zh: 这些都非常合理。

sentences.en: These are all really sensible.
sentences.zh: 然而，它们中的许多也依赖于我们的认知能力，而这些能力只有在我们处于“绿色休息与消化”模式时才更容易调动。

sentences.en: However, a lot of them also draw on our cognitive faculties, and these are more available to us when we are in our green rest and digest mode.
sentences.zh: 当然，当我们处于交感神经系统时，我们的思维会切换到那种更紧迫、更僵化、更非黑即白的模式。

sentences.en: Of course, our thinking switches gear into that more urgent, more rigid, more black and white type of place when we are in our sympathetic nervous system.
sentences.zh: 当我们处于背侧关闭状态时，我们很难有任何创造性思维，也很难找到解决办法或摆脱这种困境的方法。

sentences.en: And we really struggle a lot when we're in dorsal shutdown to have any ability to have creative thought or ability to have solutions or ways to start moving out of this stuckness.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在书中提出的观点以及我提供的工具，都是为了尝试安抚神经系统，使其回到那个状态，因为是的，绝对地，

sentences.en: So my argument in my book and where I provide tools is to try and soothe the nervous system to get back to that place because, yes, absolutely,
sentences.zh: 从长远来看我们需要这些东西，但它们可能无法立即生效。

sentences.en: in the long term we need those things, but they might not be immediately available.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经有了一些自己使用的工具。

sentences.en: And you might already have tools that you use.
sentences.zh: 这些通常是用于平静身心的躯体类工具。

sentences.en: These are often somatic type of tools for calming.
sentences.zh: 我现在就把手放在心口，因为呼吸、用手安抚自己以及运动都是很好的方法。

sentences.en: So my hands are on my heart right now because breathing, using your hands to soothe yourself and using movement.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你已经掌握了这些工具，请确保尽可能频繁地使用它们。

sentences.en: So if you already have tools up your sleeve for those, make sure you're using them as frequently as you can.
sentences.zh: 在未来的某一集中，我会谈谈在一天中的某些过渡点进行这些练习。

sentences.en: And in a future one of these episodes, I talk about doing that at certain transition points in the day.
sentences.zh: 那么，我要结束这一集了，希望它真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: So I'm going to sign this episode off, and I hope it's been really helpful.
sentences.zh: 我将在下一集中与你见面，届时我将开始讨论倦怠的三种不同亚型。

sentences.en: I'm going to meet you in the next one where I'm going to start talking about the three different subtypes of burnout.
sentences.zh: 你会想听听这个的，因为当我了解到这一点时，对我来说真是一个醍醐灌顶的时刻。

sentences.en: You're going to want to hear that because it was a real penny drop moment for me when I learned about this.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，克莱尔。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Claire.
sentences.zh: 这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: That was absolutely wonderful.
sentences.zh: 如果这引起了你的兴趣，请务必查看我节目说明中关于这本书的详细信息。

sentences.zh: 请务必在社交媒体上与我联系。

sentences.zh: 让我知道你对这一集的看法。

sentences.zh: 也去关注克莱尔吧，她在各处的账号都是克莱尔·普拉姆利博士。

sentences.en: And come and follow Claire too, where she is Dr. Claire Plumley everywhere.
sentences.zh: 加入免费的Facebook群组“有抱负的心理学家社区与玛丽安·特伦特博士”，

sentences.en: Come and join the free Facebook group, the Aspiring Psychologist Community with Dr. Marianne Trent,
sentences.zh: 这里是每周举办的“玛丽安的心态与动力”课程的独家基地。

sentences.en: which is the exclusive home of Marianne's Mindset and Motivation sessions, which happen weekly.
sentences.zh: 如果你发现自己目前有更多空闲时间，除了阅读克莱尔博士的书，你可能还会发现《有抱负的心理学家合集》一书

sentences.en: If you're finding you've got a little bit more time on your hands at the moment, as well as reading Dr. Claire's book, you might well find the Aspiring Psychologist Collective book
sentences.zh: 和《临床心理学家合集》一书很有用。

sentences.en: and the Clinical Psychologist Collective book useful.
sentences.zh: 所以一定要去看看。

sentences.en: So do check those out.
sentences.zh: 如果你读过它们，请花点时间在亚马逊或Goodreads上给我写条评论，因为这确实有助于书籍触及更广泛的读者群。

sentences.zh: 也请花点时间关注、订阅本节目，你可以在Spotify、Apple Podcasts以及YouTube上进行操作。

sentences.en: Please do also take a moment to follow, subscribe to the show, which you can do on Spotify, on Apple Podcasts and, of course, YouTube.
sentences.zh: 对于任何你非常喜欢的播客来说，这真的是你能做的最贴心的事。

sentences.en: It really is the kindest thing you can do for any podcast that you are a big fan of.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，它是完全免费的。

sentences.en: And, of course, it is totally free.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你的时间。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 我很期待为你带来下一集，它将于周六上午10点在YouTube上发布，并于周一上午6点在各大播客平台上线。

sentences.en: I will look forward to bringing you the next episode, which will be along for you on Saturday at 10am on YouTube and wherever you get your podcasts from 6am on Monday.
sentences.zh: 善待自己，非常感谢你成为我世界的一部分。

sentences.en: Stay kind to you and thank you so much for being part of my world.
sentences.zh: 如果你想成为一名心理学家，那就让这成为你的指南吧。

sentences.en: If you're looking to become a psychologist, then let this be your guide.
sentences.zh: 有这个播客在身边，你离获得资格就不远了。

sentences.en: With this podcast at your side, you'll be on your way to being qualified.
sentences.zh: 这是玛丽安·特伦特博士的《有抱负的心理学家》播客。

sentences.en: It's the Aspiring Psychologist podcast with Dr. Marianne Trent.
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚到除了出卖时间换取金钱之外的收入，会怎样？

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性的收入来源。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我有个好消息要宣布。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One2Many program is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships and digital products.
sentences.zh: 我自己曾在2022年完成了该项目，此后也支持了两批心理学家走过他们的旅程。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖励，以及我提供的独家支持套餐，无需额外费用。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四次小组智囊团会议、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特纳姆和梅森的礼品，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalised guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 通过描述中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时为你解答。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时为你解答。
